newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria cenbank says any rate move will be down.
newsitem.headline: Austria cenbank says any rate move will be down.

text.p: Austrian central bank director Adolf Wala said on Friday any rate move in the foreseeable future would be down, adding a cut in the money market rate may be possible in the first quarter of 1997.
"We don't expect a change in interest rates in the next few weeks," he told Reuters in an interview. "If there's any move, it will be down."
He said a possible cut would first be made in the Gomex money market rate "towards the end of the first quarter" and later also in the discount rate.
"Inflation remains under control and I think there would be room to give the economy a little signal if the price discipline is maintained," Wala said.
Austria's inflation rate stood at 2.1 percent in October, up slightly from 2.0 percent in September.

The Austrian discount rate was cut by 50 basis points to a historic low of 2.5 percent on April 18. The Gomex money market rate was cut by 10 basis points to 3.40 percent on August 22. The Lombard emergency borrowing rate stands at 4.75 percent.

Austria joined the European exchange rate mechanism in January 1995. It has closely followed Germany's monetary lead since the schilling was pegged to the mark almost two decades ago. -- Knut Engelmann, Vienna newsroom +431 53112 274
